title: Hold back a misleading term
statement: Hold back a technical term whose everyday meaning misleads until the concept it names is needed, then define it at once against that everyday meaning.
example: One card keeps two genetics terms out of grades 3-5, then defines them at once against their everyday sense in grades 6-8.
detail: The biology misconception card keeps 'dominant' and 'recessive' out of grades 3-5, because the terms carry too much everyday baggage and the concepts are not needed yet. When the terms arrive in grades 6-8, it defines them immediately with the anti-misconception framing that dominant does not mean stronger, better or more common.
against: One example: the card says this of one pair of terms.
